core_obligations: Apply the lifting property inductively along the displayed diagrams to construct compatible maps from S to each quotient R/I^n (proof lines 41484-41500).
Use uniqueness in the lifting property to see that the compositions S/J^n to R/I^n to S/J^n are the identity (proof lines 41501-41503).
Conclude that the induced maps on the quotients, and hence on the associated graded rings, are isomorphisms (proof lines 41501-41505).
proof_roadmap: Build the compatible dotted arrows in the three displayed lifting diagrams (proof lines 41483-41500).
Get the isomorphisms on the quotients from uniqueness in the lifting property (proof lines 41501-41505).
difficulty_reason: If R to S is formally etale and R to S/J is surjective with kernel I, the lemma states that each R/I^n is isomorphic to S/J^n and that the associated graded rings agree (statement lines 41473-41481). The proof does not compute with generators of I or J: it displays three lifting diagrams representing the induction, obtains compatible dotted maps into the successive quotients, and then uses uniqueness in the lifting property to see that the resulting maps compose to the identity (proof lines 41483-41505). Running the lifting property up the tower and then invoking uniqueness is the whole argument, and the diagrams carry the induction explicitly. H2.
